record.paper_title: Some open problems in spectral theory
record.context_brief: Open level sets of the resolvent norm
record.original_question: Let A be a bounded linear operator on a Banach space X, and consider the resolvent norm function λ -> ||(A - λI)^(-1)|| on the resolvent set of A. Can a level set {λ in C : ||(A - λI)^(-1)|| = 1/ε} contain a nonempty open subset, equivalently can the resolvent norm take a finite constant value throughout an open set?

evidence.quote: Let A : X → X be a bounded linear operator on a Banach space X. J. Globevnik 1976, A. Böttcher 1994: Can the level set {λ ∈ C : k(A − λI)−1 k = 1/ε} have an open subset? Can k(A − λI)−1 k take a finite constant value on an open set?
ES 2008: Yes ES and S. Shkarin 2009: Yes, even if X is separable, reflexive and strictly convex.

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let $X$ be a complex Banach space and let $A : X \to X$ be a bounded linear operator. The resolvent set of $A$ is $\rho(A) = \{\lambda \in \mathbb{C} : A - \lambda I \text{ is invertible}\}$, and on $\rho(A)$ one defines the resolvent norm function $\lambda \mapsto \|(A - \lambda I)^{-1}\|$, where $\|\cdot\|$ is the operator norm on $\mathcal{B}(X)$. For a given $\varepsilon > 0$, consider the level set $\{\lambda \in \mathbb{C} : \|(A - \lambda I)^{-1}\| = 1/\varepsilon\}$. Does there exist such an operator $A$ on some Banach space $X$ for which this level set contains a nonempty open subset of $\mathbb{C}$? Equivalently, can the function $\lambda \mapsto \|(A - \lambda I)^{-1}\|$ take a finite constant value on a nonempty open subset of $\rho(A)$? Furthermore, can such an example be constructed when $X$ is required to be separable, reflexive, and strictly convex?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem has been solved affirmatively. E. Shargorodsky (2008) constructed a bounded operator on a Banach space whose resolvent norm is constant on a nonempty open set, and Shargorodsky and S. Shkarin (2009) strengthened this to operators on separable, reflexive, strictly convex Banach spaces.

status_evidence.title: On the level sets of the resolvent norm of a linear operator
status_evidence.snippet: Shargorodsky shows that the resolvent norm of a bounded operator on a Banach space can be constant on an open set, answering the question of Globevnik and Böttcher.
status_evidence.claim: A bounded linear operator on a Banach space can have resolvent norm constant on a nonempty open set.

status_evidence.title: The level sets of the resolvent norm and convexity properties of Banach spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Shargorodsky and Shkarin show such examples exist even on separable, reflexive and strictly convex Banach spaces.
status_evidence.claim: The phenomenon persists on separable, reflexive, strictly convex Banach spaces.
